title: SLI backfill strategy and trace sampling guardrails
body:
Summary:

This is a working plan for how we backfill SLIs for newly instrumented signals and how we apply runtime trace-sampling guardrails to keep query costs predictable while preserving investigation fidelity. The doc combines a short policy, a concrete backfill recipe, dashboard implications, and a set of incremental tasks for Q4 instrumentation sprints.

Why this matters:
- We regularly add SLI variants and metrics (kv-warmth, ttf-token, model-fanout-count) but lack a consistent backfill path for historical baselines. That slows rollouts and makes canary comparisons noisy.
- Unbounded trace capture during backfills or debug probes exploded costs last quarter; we need guardrails to avoid repeating that.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Provide a repeatable backfill checklist to generate 90/95/99 SLI baselines for 30/90/180 day views.
- Define trace-sampling thresholds and escalation policies to balance cost vs. investigation needs.
- Codify dashboard templates and annotation practices so backfilled SLIs integrate cleanly with rollout gates.
- Produce a small tooling script to replay sampled traces for synthetic canaries.

Principles:
- Conservative retention: prioritize aggregated SLI baselines over full-trace retention unless an investigation is open.
- Tenant-respect: when backfilling multi-tenant metrics, do not surface tenant-identifying attributes in high-cardinality rollups.
- Versioned baselines: link each backfilled baseline to model version and rollout tag.

Backfill recipe (stepwise):
1) Scope and quick audit (owners + expected cardinality): identify metric(s), typical cardinality (per-tenant/per-route), and expected storage cost. Note any PII/PHI concerns.
2) Light sampling collect window (7 days): enable 1% full-trace sampling + 10% header-only sampling across traffic for the metric.
3) Augmented probe window (30 days) for low-traffic routes: increase header-only to 25% and full-trace to 2% only for routes flagged as low-volume.
4) Aggregation job run: run nightly jobs to compute 50/90/95/99 quantiles and histograms; store results in metrics-store with a backfill tag.
5) Backfill validation: compare aggregated histograms vs. synthetics (if available) and flag >10% delta for manual review.
6) Promote to dashboard: create a backfilled SLI tile and add a provenance note (backfill window, sampling rates, job id).
7) Sunset sampling: after baseline established, revert runtime sampling to steady-state (see steady-state defaults below).

Runtime trace-sampling guardrails (policy):
- Default steady-state: 0.5% full-trace capture across production requests; 5% header-only sampling (trace metadata plus span counts).
- Critical routes: for routes with SLO < 200ms or high error sensitivity (payment, auth), default to 2% full-trace capture, 20% header-only. Requires owner sign-off.
- Incident mode: automated bump to 5% full-trace for affected route(s) for up to 6 hours, with cost alert threshold at 1.5x expected daily trace spend.
- Backfill mode (see recipe): temporary elevated windows with explicit end-dates and Jira ticket linking.

Sampling heuristics: what to keep vs drop:
- Keep traces with: status != 200, anomalous latency > p99 + 50ms, kv-cache eviction events, model-fanout > 1, hallucination-detection flag (if instrumented).
- Enrich header-only samples with minimal context tags (route, model-version, tenant-shard) but avoid free-form prompt tokens.

Dashboard and alert implications:
- Each backfilled SLI must have a provenance badge: "backfilled - 2025-10-08..2025-11-06 - sample=1%/10%" (example).
- Rollout gates: dashboards used for canary must show both live SLI and backfilled baseline lines and use a shaded band to indicate sampling uncertainty (computed from bootstrap on sampled traces).
- Alerting: temporarily mute automated SLI alerts for metrics that are in backfill windows to avoid alert storms; instead create a "backfill monitoring" alert with a higher threshold to catch gross regressions.

Operational runbook snippets:
- If trace-cost alert fires during backfill: immediately revert sampling to steady-state, page obs-oncall, and open a cost investigation ticket.
- If backfill validation delta > 10%: stop backfill, reduce sampling to header-only, and kick off manual audit (owner + applied-ml).

Tooling wishlist (MVP first):
- small CLI: obs-backfill run --metric kv-warmth --window 2025-10-01:2025-10-31 --sampling 2% --tag backfill-2025-oct -> submits sampling config + nightly aggregation job + generates provenance note.
- dashboard helper that computes and renders sampling uncertainty band from sampled histogram.
- replay harness to synthesize full traces from header-only samples for small cohorts.

Permissions and cost accounting:
- Backfills require a billing cap set on the sampling job (default $500 per backfill task) and must list budget owner.
- Any elevated sampling that crosses the billing cap requires approval from Observability manager and Finance.

Open questions / risk register:
- How to estimate sampling uncertainty for rare events (p99 of rare error classes)? (PRI: high)
- Do we allow tenant-level backfills that temporarily surface tenant ids in traces for debugging? (privacy/legal)
- How to best annotate dashboards so SREs can trust backfilled baselines during fast canaries?

Concrete next actions (short sprint):
- [ ] Diego: prototype obs-backfill CLI skeleton and sampling job submission flow (due 2026-02-14).
- [ ] Priya: draft dashboard provenance badge components and uncertainty shading rules (due 2026-02-21).
- [ ] Liam: run safety review with privacy team on tenant-level backfill cases (due 2026-02-18).
- [ ] Ava: create JIRA epic and link Confluence page for long-form policy (done: CONFLUENCE-OBS-1498).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a small "trace escrow" store where full traces from backfills are locked and require explicit access for 30 days.
- Could use synthetic canary replays to bootstrap baselines for very low-volume routes instead of high sampling.

References and links:
- CONFLUENCE-OBS-1498 (backfill decision record), JIRA-OPS-877 (cost overrun incident log), GH PR #432 (sampling controller changes).

Status: draft. This doc will evolve as prototypes come in.
summary_short: Working plan for SLI backfill + trace sampling guardrails to limit cost and preserve investigation fidelity
